text: dsh-peak 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 网页端的价格时段插件：它在输入框旁显示高峰或非高峰状态与下一次切换倒计时，并注册 dsh_peak_status 工具供 agent 查询当前 UTC、北京时间、计价状态和切换时间。插件按工作日时段、周末及中国法定节假日分类，适合希望判断 DeepSeek API 何时处于高峰计价、安排长任务时机的用户。无需 API 密钥或额外外部服务。

dsh-peak shows DeepSeek API peak and off-peak windows in the DSH web composer, with a countdown to the next change. Its dsh_peak_status tool reports pricing state, UTC and Beijing times, holiday status, and next switch. It helps users check pricing before long jobs. No API key is needed.
想知道现在 DeepSeek API 是不是高峰价格，以及还要多久切换。
能不能在 DSH 输入框旁显示当前高峰或非高峰时段？
Show me whether DeepSeek API pricing is at peak right now and when it changes.
dsh-peak 的功能「价格状态与切换倒计时」：网页输入框旁显示 PEAK 或 OFF-PEAK 标记及倒计时；agent 也可调用 dsh_peak_status 获取当前时段、北京时间、节假日原因和下一次切换。

dsh-peak README · dsh-peak：A live **peak/off-peak pricing indicator** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), shipped as an installable dual-face bundle.

DeepSeek's API moved to peak/off-peak pricing on **2026-08-16 16:00 UTC**: during peak windows the rate is **2× the off-peak rate**, and the windows line up almost exactly with Chinese work hours. Weekends and Chinese statutory holidays are billed off-peak **all day**. This plugin makes that visible:

dsh-peak README · dsh-peak：- **Composer pill** (browser): a small always-visible control at the left of the input row — **red "PEAK"** during peak windows, **green "OFF-PEAK"** otherwise, with a live countdown to the next switch and a hover tooltip showing UTC + Beijing times and the reason the day is off-peak.
- **`dsh_peak_status` tool** (host): the agent can call it before suggesting or running long/expensive work, so it can warn you when you're about to pay the peak rate.

dsh-peak README · Pricing windows：Peak applies on days that are neither a weekend nor a Chinese statutory holiday:

| Window | Beijing | UTC |
|---|---|---|
| Peak 1 | 09:00–12:00 weekdays | 01:00–04:00 |
| Peak 2 | 14:00–18:00 weekdays | 06:00–10:00 |
| Off-peak | everything else | — (half of peak) |

Whole-day off-peak, since **2026-08-23 00:00 Beijing**:

dsh-peak README · Pricing windows：| Day | Rule |
|---|---|
| Saturday + Sunday | off-peak all day, including make-up workdays (调休) that fall on a weekend |
| Chinese statutory holidays | off-peak all day (DeepSeek notice of 2026-09-19) |

dsh-peak README · Pricing windows：Holidays follow the State Council's annual arrangement ([国办发明电〔2025〕7号](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202511/content_7047091.htm)). The 2026 table covers Mid-Autumn (Sep 25) and National Day (Oct 1–7), which — with the Sep 20 and Oct 10 make-up weekends — make Sep 20 to Oct 10, 2026 almost entirely off-peak.

dsh-peak README · Holiday data：`core.js` holds the whole-day rules: `HOLIDAYS` (inclusive Beijing date ranges, listed only from the 2026-09-19 notice onward), `MAKEUP_WORKDAYS` (labels only — a make-up workday is off-peak because it is a weekend), and `HOLIDAY_CALENDAR_THROUGH`, the last date the table covers. The State Council publishes the next year's arrangement each November, so update all three when it lands; until then the tool appends a warning to its summary and the pill's tooltip, because holidays after that date would be misreported as peak.

dsh-peak README · Holiday data：Both halves run the same code: `index.js` imports `core.js`, while the browser bundle embeds the marked region from `core.js` verbatim (a bundle is served as one script and cannot import a sibling module).

dsh-peak README · Requirements：- A DeepSeek Harness **web profile** (the pill mounts in the browser; the tool registers host-side)
- No runtime dependencies — the host half uses a raw `ctx.tools.register` definition and the client bundle's only external is `react`

dsh-peak README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-peak            # once published to npm
dsh plugin --profile web add github:geokkjer/dsh-peak   # or straight from this repo
```

Or from a local checkout of this repo:

```sh
cd /path/to/dsh-peak
dsh plugin --profile web add .
```

dsh-peak README · Install：`dsh plugin` runs `pnpm add` in the profile directory and registers the package as a bundle layer (`dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`). After the next `dsh web` restart, both halves activate: the host row registers `dsh_peak_status`, and the `dsh.client` declaration makes the browser roster serve `/plugins/dsh-peak/client.js`, mounting the pill in every session.

dsh-peak README · Usage：Ask the agent:

- *"is it peak pricing right now?"* → calls `dsh_peak_status`
- *"run this long job off-peak"* → the agent checks `dsh_peak_status` first and reports the window

The pill itself needs no interaction: it self-updates every 30s and flips color at each window boundary.

dsh-peak README · Usage：`dsh_peak_status` returns the `summary` an agent reads plus structured fields: `peak`, `offPeakReason` (`weekend` / `holiday` / `none`, the last when only the peak-window rule applies), `holidayName` (empty unless the day is a holiday), `makeupWorkday`, the UTC and Beijing clocks, `nextSwitchUtc` / `nextSwitchInMinutes`, and `holidayCalendarThrough` / `holidayCalendarStale`.

dsh-peak README · Usage：Tool schemas use the harness's JSON-schema subset, which takes a single `type` string per node — a `type` array disables the whole plugin entry at load, so `offPeakReason` carries the `none` sentinel instead of a nullable type.

dsh-peak README · Development：The repo is deliberately build-free: `core.js`, `index.js` (host tool), and `client.js` (browser bundle in the module-loader format) are committed plain ESM, so `pnpm add` works with no `prepare` step.

```sh
npm run sync:client   # after editing core.js: refresh the region embedded in client.js
npm test
```

dsh-peak README · Development：`npm test` runs the smoke suite: host identity + tool registration, window and whole-day classification at known instants (09:46 UTC → peak; 05:00 UTC → off-peak; Mid-Autumn and National Day → off-peak all day, including the switch that skips the whole National Day break; make-up workday weekends), a check that `client.js` still embeds the current `core.js`, and client bundle materialization against a stubbed module loader + React.
